result:
Rain on a tin roof has a particular kind of music—staccato, relentless, almost percussive. I love lying in bed and listening to it, especially when the rest of the house is quiet. There's something about that sound that makes the world feel smaller, cozier, more manageable.

This week brought a lot of rain where I live, the kind that turns backyard puddles into small ponds and sends the cat bolting under the bed every time the sky cracks open. I spent an afternoon rearranging bookshelves that didn't really need rearranging, just because the weather made the indoors feel like the only sensible place to be.

I've been thinking a lot about how seasons shape our inner lives. Winter asks us to slow down, to hibernate, to burrow into blankets and books. Spring will arrive soon, I hope, and with it the restless energy of wanting to be outside until the sun finally goes down. But for now, the rain has given me permission to be still.

I've also been cooking more. Nothing fancy—soups, pasta, roasted vegetables. There's comfort in the ritual of chopping onions and letting the kitchen fill with that sharp, bright smell. My partner says my soups are too salty, and they're probably right, but I like the boldness of it. Life is too short for bland broth.

Maybe tomorrow the sun will come out. Maybe I'll go for a walk. But tonight, the rain is enough.
